name: Orbis
description: Orbis ad blocking for the Orbis browser (a hidden component of the browser). The new tab page, search results and panel are built into the browser (chrome://orbis*).
//host_permissions: <all_urls> is here for one reason: Chromium's capture check accepts only the literal <all_urls> pattern or activeTab. 'http://*/*' plus 'https://*/*' is the same web access in every other respect, but URLPattern::MatchesAllURLs() is true only for the literal pattern, so Visual Search's picture of the page was refused with 'Either the <all_urls> or activeTab permission is required' -- and activeTab is granted only when somebody invokes the extension itself, which a Ctrl-drag on a page is not. The http/https patterns are kept because they are what the content scripts match.

rule_resources.//: The first line, and the reason it is first. Chromium indexes a ruleset before any of it bites, and 114,000 rules take seconds on every launch -- so for those seconds the browser was fetching ads it was about to start blocking. A few hundred rules index in milliseconds, and rulesets are indexed independently, so this one is enforcing while the big ones are still being read. It is almost entirely a subset of them: what changes is when, not what.

content_scripts.//: The selection orb. Runs in the isolated world so a page can neither see it nor reach it, and in every frame so a selection inside an iframe gets one too. document_idle: nothing here is needed before the page has drawn.

Orbis Visual Search. Isolated world, so a page can neither see it nor reach it, and the top frame only: the capture is of the whole window, and a cross-origin frame cannot know where it sits inside it. document_idle: the gesture is not needed before the page has drawn.
